title: The curbside pause
question: What happens in the next five seconds?
context: A pedestrian stands beside the curb. A parked van blocks part of the view. The camera vehicle is approaching the crossing.

options.text: The pedestrian stays beside the curb.
The pedestrian steps into the crossing.
The pedestrian walks away along the sidewalk.

outcome: The pedestrian steps into the crossing.
explanation: In this storyboard, standing at the curb is followed by a crossing. The parked van limits what can be seen. One continuation does not prove a person's intention in another scene.

evidence.text: The pedestrian is at the edge of the sidewalk.
The pedestrian enters the marked crossing.
The pedestrian continues across the camera vehicle's path.

title: Beside the bus stop
question: What does the pedestrian do next?
context: A pedestrian stands near the road beside a bus-stop sign. A bus approaches on the near lane. No crossing is visible yet.

options.text: They remain on the sidewalk as the bus arrives.
They cross in front of the approaching bus.
They walk into the opposite lane.

outcome: The pedestrian remains on the sidewalk.
explanation: The continuation shows waiting, not crossing. Being close to a road alone does not establish what someone will do. This drill contrasts with The curbside pause.

evidence.text: A pedestrian stands beside a bus-stop sign.
The bus draws alongside the stop.
The pedestrian is still on the sidewalk.

title: At the aisle junction
question: Which interaction appears in the continuation?
context: A worker approaches an aisle junction. A warehouse vehicle approaches the same junction from another direction. Racking obscures the corner.

options.text: Both continue on separate paths without interacting.
The vehicle turns away before the junction.
The worker pauses as the vehicle passes the junction.

outcome: The worker pauses while the vehicle passes.
explanation: The storyboard shows an interaction at the junction, followed by a pause. It does not establish a collision, distance, speed, or an actual near-miss classification.

evidence.text: Two paths approach the same aisle junction.
The worker stops at the junction.
The vehicle passes in front of the stationary worker.

title: A gap in the queue
question: What changes in the next segment?
context: Several vehicles form a dense queue. A gap opens ahead of one car while neighboring lanes remain crowded.

options.text: The car advances into the gap and stops again.
The car exits across two lanes.

outcome: The car advances, then stops again.
explanation: A short movement within a queue is different from sustained free-flow traffic. The schematic illustrates stop-and-go motion without claiming calibrated speeds or causes of congestion.

evidence.text: A gap opens in the middle lane.
One car moves into the gap.
The car stops behind the next vehicle.

title: The narrow doorway
question: How does the doorway interaction unfold?
context: Two people approach a narrow doorway from opposite sides. One carries a large object. Both are still approaching.

options.text: One pauses while the person carrying the object passes.
Both turn away from the doorway.

outcome: One person pauses to let the other pass.
explanation: The continuation shows a pause and sequential passage. No identity, intent, or exact occupancy count is inferred from the interaction.

evidence.text: Two people approach the same narrow doorway.
One person pauses beside the doorway.
The person carrying the object passes through first.

title: The parked car
question: What changes in the next five seconds?
context: A car is parked beside a neighborhood street. Another vehicle passes on the road. The parked car has not moved in the observation window.

options.text: A pedestrian crosses directly in front of it.
The parked car pulls out into the road.

outcome: The parked car pulls out into the road.
explanation: This illustrative continuation shows a change from stationary to moving. A fixed-camera archive can supply these ordinary transitions without needing an accident or an unusual event.

evidence.text: The car remains beside the curb.
The car begins leaving its parked position.
The car is moving along the roadway.
